bullets: Purpose: **exposition**; establishes Scrooge’s character and the attitudes Dickens attacks.
Turning point: Marley’s warning that ‘Mankind was my business’.
core.p: Christmas Eve. Scrooge, a cold, mean moneylender, rejects his nephew Fred’s invitation, refuses the charity collectors, begrudges his clerk Bob Cratchit a day off, and goes home. Marley’s face appears in the door knocker; Marley’s ghost, wrapped in chains, warns him he will be visited by three spirits.

bullets: Purpose: explains **why** Scrooge became cold; evokes sympathy.
Turning point: Scrooge weeps and begins to regret (he wishes he had given something to a carol singer; he thinks of Bob).
core.h: Stave 2: The First of the Three Spirits
core.p: The Ghost of Christmas Past shows Scrooge his lonely childhood at school, his sister Fan rescuing him, Fezziwig’s joyful Christmas ball, and Belle breaking their engagement because ‘another idol’, money, has replaced her. Finally Belle, now married with children. Scrooge begs to be shown no more and extinguishes the Ghost’s light.

bullets: Purpose: shows **how others live** now; the warmth Scrooge excludes himself from.
Turning point: Scrooge asks if Tiny Tim will live; his own ‘surplus population’ words are thrown back at him.
core.h: Stave 3: The Second of the Three Spirits
core.p: The Ghost of Christmas Present, a jolly giant surrounded by a feast, shows Scrooge the bustling Christmas streets, the Cratchits’ joyful dinner and Tiny Tim, miners, lighthouse keepers and sailors celebrating, and Fred’s party. At the end the Ghost reveals Ignorance and Want beneath its robe.

bullets: Turning point: ‘I will honour Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.’
core.h: Stave 4: The Last of the Spirits
core.p: The silent, hooded Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come shows businessmen joking about a dead man, thieves selling his possessions to Old Joe, a couple relieved by his death, the Cratchits mourning Tiny Tim, and finally a neglected grave with Scrooge’s name. Scrooge begs for the chance to change.

bullets: Purpose: **resolution**; models the change Dickens hopes for in readers.
Cyclical: mirrors Stave 1 (Fred, the charity collector, Bob), now reversed.
core.p: Scrooge wakes on Christmas morning, joyful. He sends a prize turkey to the Cratchits, gives a large donation to the charity collector, goes to Fred’s party, raises Bob’s salary, and becomes a ‘second father’ to Tiny Tim, who did not die.

callouts.p: Stave 5 deliberately repeats Stave 1’s encounters so that the reader can measure Scrooge’s transformation.

model: Past: school; Fan; Fezziwig; Belle’s break-up; Belle’s family
Present: streets; Cratchits; miners/lighthouse/ship; Fred’s party; Ignorance and Want
Yet to Come: businessmen; Old Joe; the couple in debt; Cratchits mourning; the grave
exam.q: Quick recall: list the scenes each Ghost shows, in order.
exam.tip: Accurate references across the whole text are essential for part (b).

mistakes.r: Past: school, Fan, Fezziwig, Belle. Present: Cratchits, Fred, Ignorance and Want. Future: dead man, Old Joe, Tiny Tim’s death, grave.
mistakes.w: Mixing up which Ghost shows which scenes.

quotes.a: Gothic, comic opening; death frames the story.
quotes.q: Marley was dead: to begin with.
I will honour Christmas in my heart

quotes.a: Physical lightness = spiritual freedom from chains.
quotes.q: I am as light as a feather

summary: A stave-by-stave summary of A Christmas Carol and its five-part structure: Scrooge’s cold present, the past, the present, the future and his transformation, with the key turning points to use in part (b) answers.

terms.d: The opening that introduces characters and situation.
The point of greatest tension (Stave 4 at the grave).
The ending where conflicts are resolved.
